title: Principality of Mingrelia
capsule: Mingrelia (Georgian: სამეგრელო, Samegrelo; also Odishi) was a western Georgian principality ruled by the Dadiani dynasty from the breakup of the unified Kingdom of Georgia in the fifteenth century. Emerging as an autonomous polity around 1466–1469, it maintained persistent rivalry with neighbouring Abkhazia and Guria while enduring repeated Ottoman pressure and the slave trade, which devastated its population across the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The principality formally accepted Russian suzerainty under Grigol Dadiani in 1803 and was administered as a vassal under its native rulers until the Russian Empire abolished the dynasty and annexed it directly in 1867; the attestation end-date of 1811 reflects the formal consolidation of Russian administrative control rather than the extinction of the Dadiani title. The principality is notable as a survival of medieval Georgian feudal structures into the early modern period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Political history and dynasty are well attested in Georgian chronicles and Russian administrative records, but pre-nineteenth-century territorial boundaries are reconstructed from narrative sources and lack precise cartographic corroboration.
